imagePurpose: Generic AI representative product imagery; supplier appearance and specifications may vary.

finalPrompts.prompt: Create a photorealistic commercial product photograph of ONE fully erected straight tuck-end folding paperboard carton on a seamless pure white studio background. It must look like a real professionally manufactured retail carton photographed with a camera. Compact rectangular carton in plain matte warm-white paperboard, broad front and narrower side, body squared up with four coherent walls and a clean bottom already tucked shut. One top tuck lid is partly raised, with its terminal tuck tongue and two small side dust flaps visible; keep the rest of the carton assembled. Straight tuck construction: both end closures fold toward the same rear face, although the closed bottom need not be exposed. Three-quarter front view from slightly above, soft natural contact shadow, subtle paper grain and slight authentic crease compression at folded corners, clean thin card edges. Landscape 4:3. Product occupies about 80–85 percent image height with safe margins. Empty carton. NO flat blank, unfolded wall strip, accordion structure, dieline, schematic, transparent walls, exploded view or extra detached parts. No printed text, logos, watermarks, dimensions, decorations, labels, contents or hands. Use photographic material realism and physically simple carton construction; do not try to display both end mechanisms at once.

Create a photorealistic commercial product photograph of ONE fully erected reverse tuck-end retail folding carton made from unprinted natural brown kraft paperboard, standing upright on a seamless pure white studio background. A believable manufactured folding carton with four square, coherent walls, broad front and narrow side; modest tall rectangular proportions like a small retail product box. The bottom is fully tucked closed and supporting the carton. The top main tuck lid is partly open, with one rounded tuck tongue and two small dust flaps hinged from the narrow sidewalls. Reverse tuck construction means top and bottom closures hinge from opposite broad faces; the closed bottom may remain out of sight. Three-quarter front view, slightly above eye level, real fine kraft-paper fibres, restrained crease marks, normal thin card edges, gentle natural shadow and diffuse photographic studio lighting. Landscape 4:3 with entire carton visible, filling about 82 percent image height and safe margins. Empty interior. NO flat unfolded blank, accordion, dieline, blueprint, cutaway, exploded form, detached panels or impossible extra folds. No printing, text, logo, watermark, certification mark, price, arbitrary dimension or hands. Prioritize a real assembled box, not exposing every structural detail.

Create a photorealistic studio catalogue photograph of ONE fully erected plain matte white paperboard folding carton with a CLOSED manually interlocked snap-lock 1-2-3 bottom, photographed resting on its long side with the bottom face gently angled toward the camera. Real manufactured compact rectangular retail carton, four straight coherent walls, empty interior, thin smooth non-corrugated paperboard. The visible closed base is made from four die-cut flaps fitted together: broad overlapping closure panels with a small tongue seated into a receiving notch and two tucked side locking flaps. Show a restrained plausible interlocking seam on a flat closed bottom. It must not be a pre-glued diagonal auto-lock/crash-lock base. The opposite tuck top can be closed. Three-quarter view, subtle real paper grain and compressed fold creases, soft neutral contact shadow, diffuse camera studio lighting, seamless pure white background. Landscape 4:3 composition, all edges fully visible with safe margins, carton fills about 85 percent image width. NO unfolded blank, exploded view, open bottom wings, diagrams, arrows, detached pieces, labels, printed text, logos, watermarks, contents, certification stamps, dimension markings, people or hands. A real-looking assembled carton is more important than displaying every flap.

reviewLimits: STE/RTE closed bottoms are out of sight; photos do not verify exact closure orientation. Snap-lock form is illustrative; supplier dieline, assembly and load suitability remain unconfirmed.
